claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are specific rules that apply. You can still qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over if they are under 20 and stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending sixth form, college, or doing an apprenticeship?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He left school recently, but he has signed up with the local careers service to help figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is helpful.

According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

**How long ago did Alex register with the careers service?** I need to know if it's been less than 20 weeks or more than 20 weeks since he registered.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's only been a couple of months since he registered - definitely less than 20 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Just to confirm a few more details to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're here in England. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Although Alex is 17 and has left education or training, you can still claim Child Benefit because he has registered with the local careers service. The rules allow Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, as long as they register with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex registered only a couple of months ago (which is well within the 20-week period), you meet the eligibility criteria. You also meet all the other requirements:
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives at home with you
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important to note:** This eligibility will last for up to 20 weeks from when Alex registered with the careers service. After that 20-week period ends, you would only continue to be eligible if Alex either:
- Returns to approved education or training, or
- Gets a job offer, or
- Remains under 20 and in approved education/training

If you haven't already claimed, you should apply as soon as possible to ensure you receive the benefit for this period.
